To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the strong coupling limit of our discretized sum of planar QCD diagrams is well-defined; (ii) it yields a nontrivial string-like object, which is a relativistic string in the limit that the discretized lattice is fine; (iii) it has a natural interpretation as the world-sheet of a relativistic string; (iv) it is a relativistic open string in the limit of fine discretization, but it is an open string only in a very special sense

the sum of large fishnet diagrams is dominated by a string with thickness of order the inverse of the 't Hoofts coupling and that the string has a tension of order the inverse square root of the 'tHooft coupling.

the sum of planer fishnet diagrams in large N_c QED on the light-conecan be expressed as a sum over all graphs on a discretized x+ - P+ lattice with the same boundary conditions as the fishnet diagrams.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fishnet sum does not converge to a string theory, but rather to a theory of pointlike constituents.

the string theory of light-cone quantised gauge theory, as it stands, is a very good approximation of the large N_c theory at strong coupling, but is still far from being an accurate representation of the full QCD theory.

, at best, the string theory of large N_c planar gauge theory is an effective theory of QCD at large N_c and large 't Hoofts coupling, and that the usual relativistictwo-dimensional string theory emerges in a limit in which all but the lowest energy states of the string are projected out.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are now able to establish a well-defined string description of large 't Hoofts QCD at large P+ and large x+ on a lattice of fixed lattice size in both directions.
the discretized string theory is a useful model for QCD at strong 'tHooft coupling, but that it is not a complete string description of large-N_c QCD.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the sum of fishnet diagrams is a good starting point for understanding how a string theory could emerge as a strong coupling description of QCD, but that it is not a string theory.
